chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Khalaf ibn Hammad, from Yahya ibn Abdullah, who said:

I was in the presence of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), and small dishes were brought to us. So he pointed with his hand to one of them and said: 'This is Shiraz al-Utun. We have taken it for the sick among us, and whoever wishes may eat it, and whoever wishes may leave it.'

key_terms.سُكُرُّجَاتٍ: Small dishes or containers for food/drink
key_terms.شِيرَازُ الْأُتُنِ: A specific type of fermented drink (yogurt water/lassi) from Shiraz

ai.seo_question: What is Shiraz al-Utun and what is its ruling in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies 'Shiraz al-Utun' as a fermented yogurt drink preserved for the ill, demonstrating the permissibility of consuming fermented dairy products in Shia jurisprudence. His casual invitation for anyone to partake or abstain highlights the drink's general purity (taharah) and lack of specific ritual restrictions, serving as a practical precedent for dietary laws regarding fermented beverages.
